findings.what: 0200's revision helper takes `perform 1 from clara.counterparties cp where cp.id = p_counterparty for update;` from inside the AFTER-UPDATE trigger on `clara.counterparty_aliases`. That gives the retirement path an alias-row -> counterparty-row lock order, which INVERTS `clara.rename_counterparty`'s counterparty-row -> alias-insert order. Two shipped human doors on the SAME counterparty now deadlock (40P01). The file's own §4 comment asserts the opposite: "The lock serialises appends PER COUNTERPARTY and touches no other relation, so it joins no lock ordering constraint". Both doors are wired in the browser — RetireCounterpartyAliasDialog is rendered per live alias by counterparty-identity-panel.tsx:135 and renameCounterparty is posted from counterparty-hygiene-panel.tsx:157 — so a human sees an untyped "deadlock detected", not a governed refusal. `p647.revisions.race` races two concurrent alias ADDS only and cannot see this.
findings.evidence: On the fresh chain (127.0.0.1:55606/clara_647r, frontier 0200): build a counterparty named A, rename A->B (mints alias A), rename B->A, so a LIVE alias carries the counterparty's own current name; then race `clara.retire_counterparty_alias(that alias)` against `clara.rename_counterparty(cp, 'RC …')` in two `clara_authenticated` sessions holding their transactions ~250 ms. Measured, 8 rounds each way: deadlocks WITH `t_counterparty_aliases_revision` enabled = 5/8; with ONLY that trigger disabled (`alter table clara.counterparty_aliases disable trigger t_counterparty_aliases_revision`) = 0/8; trigger re-enabled afterwards (pg_trigger.tgenabled = 'O'). An earlier 5-round run of the same shape gave 4/5. Postgres DETAIL captured: "deadlock detected || DETAIL: Process 34001 waits for ShareLock on transaction 5603; blocked by process 33998. Process 33998 waits for ShareLock on transaction 5602; blocked by process 34001." Pre-0200 the cycle cannot form: the live `clara.retire_counterparty_alias` body takes only `select * into a from clara.counterparty_aliases where id=p_alias for update;` and no counterparties lock (read off pg_proc.prosrc on the same rig). `clara.merge_counterparties` is NOT affected — it already locks both parties in id order (`order by cp.id for update`), so the trigger only re-takes a lock it holds.
findings.fix: Stop choosing `revision_n` under a `clara.counterparties` row lock. In `clara._append_counterparty_identity_revision`, drop the `for update` line and insert with `revision_n = (select coalesce(max(r.revision_n),0)+1 …)` wrapped in a bounded `begin … exception when unique_violation then` retry loop (3-5 attempts) against `uq_cir_counterparty_revision`, so the helper adds no wait edge to the alias/counterparty tuple graph. (An advisory lock keyed on the counterparty does NOT fix it — it re-creates the same cycle with a different lock type.) Add a red cell that races `retire_counterparty_alias` against `rename_counterparty` on a counterparty whose current name is also a live alias (produced by renaming A->B->A) and asserts no 40P01 and exactly one revision per act.

findings.what: H-20's new Add-identifier face renders `kind` as a free-text `Input` over a column with a closed three-value CHECK (`clara.client_identifiers.kind in ('tin','ssm','bank_account')`, 0007:227), and its own hint tells the human to type a value the database refuses: `ClientIdentifiers.kindHint` = "For example ssm, tin or sst." — `sst` is not admitted. `clara.add_client_identifier` (0155:426-459) maps only `unique_violation`, so every other kind raises a bare 23514 with no CLR code and no `detail.reason`; `toDialogRefusal` (components/common/dialog-refusal.tsx:45-47) then classifies it `clr: null` and paints the raw Postgres sentence. The ticket reports H-20 as done with "the CLR10 duplicate" celled; the invalid-kind arm is celled nowhere and is the one the copy steers into.
findings.evidence: On 127.0.0.1:55606/clara_647r as a real bookkeeper persona through `humanQuery`: `select clara.add_client_identifier(p_client=>…,p_kind=>'ssm',…)` -> ok; `p_kind=>'bank_account'` -> ok; `p_kind=>'sst'` -> `23514 constraint=client_identifiers_kind_check detail=- :: new row for relation "client_identifiers" violates check constraint "client_identifiers_kind_check"`; same for `'passport'` and for `'TIN'` (the door normalises the VALUE but not the kind). The duplicate arm does work: a re-send of the same normalised (kind, value) -> `CLR10 already_recorded`.
findings.fix: Replace the free-text kind `Input` with the `NativeSelect` idiom AddCounterpartyAliasDialog already uses for `origin`, offering exactly `tin` / `ssm` / `bank_account` with their own `ClientIdentifiers.kind*` labels, and rewrite `kindHint` so it never names `sst`. Add a cell asserting the control cannot submit a kind the CHECK refuses (or, if free text is wanted, give `add_client_identifier` a typed CLR10 `kind_unknown` arm naming the three admitted values and render it verbatim).

findings.where: C:\Users\zhant\Desktop\clara-wt\647\packages\db\migrations\0200_counterparty_identity_provenance.sql:744-750 (the door's client-congruence check) and :370-381 (the two-way pin CHECKs)
findings.what: `clara.add_counterparty_alias` checks client congruence for `p_source_document` only. Nothing — neither the composite FKs (firm-congruent) nor any CHECK nor the door — requires `source_extraction_id` to belong to `source_document_id`, or `source_region_id` to belong to `source_extraction_id`. So an alias on client A can pin an extraction and a region belonging to ANOTHER CLIENT's document of the same firm, and the identity detail renders them through the verbatim `KnowledgeSourceBlock`. The file's own §1 comment claims the two-way CHECKs exist so that "a stray extraction id on a human statement is provenance theatre" is impossible, and the report closes AC1 on that. (The brief's TDD seam 3 only named the cross-CLIENT document, which IS closed — CLR23 source_not_this_client — so this is the unnamed half of the same hole.) The successor contract inherits it: `aliasDoorArgs` forwards all four pins unchecked.
findings.evidence: On 127.0.0.1:55606/clara_647r, one firm with clients A and B, each with its own document + `done` extraction + region: (B1) `origin='extracted'`, document filed to B -> `CLR23 source_not_this_client` (correct). (B2) document of another firm -> `CLR23`/`23503` (correct). (B3) document filed to A + `p_source_extraction` = client B's extraction -> **accepted**. (B4) document + extraction of A + `p_source_region` = client B's region -> **accepted**. (B5) document A1 + extraction of a DIFFERENT document A2 of the same client -> **accepted**. `clara.get_counterparty_identity` then returns those rows: `[{alias:"MixedB…",doc:"docA",ext:"docB.ext(clientB)"},{alias:"MixedR…",doc:"docA",ext:"docA.ext",region:"docB.region(clientB)"},{alias:"MixedSame…",doc:"docA",ext:"docA2.ext"}]`.
findings.fix: In `clara.add_counterparty_alias`, after the existing filing check, add two typed guards: `p_source_extraction` must satisfy `exists(select 1 from clara.document_extractions e where e.id=p_source_extraction and e.document_id=p_source_document)` and `p_source_region` must satisfy `exists(select 1 from clara.document_regions g where g.id=p_source_region and g.extraction_id=p_source_extraction)`, each raising CLR10 with a named reason (e.g. `source_extraction_not_of_document` / `source_region_not_of_extraction`). Mirror both in `packages/runtime/lib/counterparty-identity.ts`'s `localAliasRefusal` and add them to `ALIAS_REFUSAL_MESSAGES`, and extend `p647.provenance.source_pins` with the three cases above.

findings.what: `localAliasRefusal`'s non-extracted branch refuses `source_not_extracted` when `input.source_document_id !== undefined`, but neither the door (0200:723-727 tests only extraction/region/field) nor `ck_counterparty_aliases_extraction_pins` (0200:370-372, likewise) refuses a document-only pin on a non-extracted origin. The module's own comment and the final report both call this a MIRROR of 0200's CHECKs; it is stricter than them. Harmless today (nothing imports the module), but the successor would locally refuse an `agent_proposed` alias carrying only a document that the door would accept.
findings.evidence: Read of `clara.add_counterparty_alias`'s live body on 127.0.0.1:55606/clara_647r: the only non-extracted guard is `if p_origin<>'extracted' and (p_source_extraction is not null or p_source_region is not null or p_source_field_path is not null)`; `pg_get_constraintdef` for `ck_counterparty_aliases_extraction_pins` is `CHECK (origin='extracted' OR (source_extraction_id IS NULL AND source_region_id IS NULL AND source_field_path IS NULL))` — `source_document_id` appears in neither.
findings.fix: Drop `|| input.source_document_id !== undefined` from the else-branch condition so the carrier matches the door, or keep it and state in the module foot (and in the successor stanza) that this one wall is deliberately stricter than 0200.

findings.what: `AgingItem.recorded_counterparty_name` is declared with a jsdoc saying the DB supplies it "when the DB supplies it". No read produces it and no component reads it — the statement panel instead resolves names through a second `loadCounterparties` pass. A field the wire can never carry invites a future caller to render `undefined` as a name.
findings.evidence: Measured on the live catalog at 127.0.0.1:55606/clara_647r: `clara._aging_core`'s prosrc has 0 occurrences of `recorded_counterparty_name` (2 of `resolution`, 1 of `recorded_counterparty_id`); `clara._statement_core` likewise 0 / 3. Repo-wide grep over `apps/web` finds the identifier only at its declaration.
findings.fix: Delete the field, or rename the comment to say plainly that no read emits it today and it is reserved for a future `_aging_core` recut.

findings.what: The three new/changed door dialogs handle their drafts three different ways: AddClientIdentifierDialog clears both fields on success (:53), SetCounterpartyIdentifiersDialog re-seeds on open via the new `onOpened` prop, and AddCounterpartyAliasDialog does neither — after a successful add, reopening re-offers the alias just recorded plus its basis, and confirming it is refused `CLR23 alias_collision`. The alias field is pre-existing behaviour, but this branch added `basis` to the same unreset state and the report cites defect 2 as having settled this class.
findings.evidence: The component holds `const [alias, setAlias] = useState("")` (:42) and `const [basis, setBasis] = useState("")` (:44) and `onConfirm={() => onSubmit(alias, origin, basis.trim() === "" ? null : basis.trim())}` (:56) with no reset on the resolved-true path and no `onOpened`; the wrapper closes the dialog on a settled success. Compare AddClientIdentifierDialog.tsx:53 `if (ok) { setKind(""); setValue(""); }`.
findings.fix: Either clear `alias` and `basis` when `onSubmit` resolves true, or pass `onOpened={() => { setAlias(""); setBasis(""); }}` the way SetCounterpartyIdentifiersDialog now does, and say which rule the three dialogs share.

findings.what: The final report says of H-34 "every count is the database's own aggregate". That is true of `clara.list_counterparty_identity` (which computes alias_count / live_alias_count / revision_count / merge_count / unsourced_alias_count in SQL) but not of the routed detail, whose three counts are `data.aliases.filter(...).length` and `data.identifier_revisions.length` in the browser. The numbers are still honest — they count rows the read actually returned, and `get_counterparty_identity` returns both collections unbounded — so this is a claim-accuracy note, not a defect.
findings.evidence: `clara.get_counterparty_identity`'s `jsonb_build_object` tail (0200:1088-1100) returns `aliases`, `identifier_revisions`, `merges`, `conflicts` and no count key; the panel derives all three displayed counts client-side at the lines above.
findings.fix: Reword the H-34 row in the report to "every count is derived from a read that ran — aggregated in SQL on the list, counted over the returned collections on the detail", or move the three detail counts into `get_counterparty_identity`'s envelope.
